$meta.title: Adopting / migrating to Fluent 2 (Fluent UI 2.0)
$meta.description: Structured guidance for adopting Fluent 2 in an EXISTING app or report — Fluent UI v8 -> v9, from another design system, replacing hardcoded values with tokens, and per-surface adoption (Power BI, Power Apps, Power Pages).
$meta.source: Microsoft Learn + react.fluentui.dev migration docs + verified npm packages (retrieved 2026-07).

packageVersionsSeen.@fluentui/react-migration-v8-v9: 9.74.3-experimental.* (shims; experimental/preview channel — verify the latest tag on npm)

v8ToV9.title: Fluent UI React v8 (@fluentui/react) -> v9 (@fluentui/react-components)
v8ToV9.summary: v9 is the code implementation of Fluent 2. Migrate incrementally, running v8 and v9 side-by-side; prefer full v9 for new code and use shims only to avoid big-bang rewrites.

packages.name: @fluentui/react-migration-v8-v9
packages.purpose: Shim components: expose a v8 props interface but render v9 underneath, for hybrid apps.

packages.name: @fluentui/react-portal-compat
packages.purpose: Makes v9 portaled surfaces (Dialog/Popover/Tooltip) themable when mounted inside a v8 tree (wrap with PortalCompatProvider).

strategy: Add a FluentProvider (v9) at the app root (or a subtree boundary) alongside the existing v8 ThemeProvider.
Bridge the theme: derive a v9 BrandVariants/theme from your v8 palette (or use createV8Theme from @fluentui/react-migration-v8-v9 to run v8 components under a v9-derived theme).
Migrate screen-by-screen or component-by-component using the v8->v9 mapping. Replace v8 imports with v9; use shims only where a full rewrite is too costly.
Wrap the app (or v8 islands) in PortalCompatProvider so v9 overlays render themed.
Prefer full v9 components for new code; treat shims as temporary. Watch bundle size (shims pull in both v8 and v9).

componentMapping.v9: Button (appearance='primary' for PrimaryButton; icon slot for IconButton)
componentMapping.notes: CompoundButton, ToggleButton, MenuButton, SplitButton also exist.
Field provides label + validation + aria wiring.
DataGrid for interactive; Table for static.
use display:flex + gap: tokens.spacing*; or a div with griffel styles.

v8ToV9.theming: Two bridges: (1) createV8Theme(brandVariants, v9Theme) from @fluentui/react-migration-v8-v9 renders v8 under a v9-derived theme; (2) generate a v9 brand theme from your existing brand color with the fluent_generate_theme MCP tool and wrap new v9 UI in FluentProvider.
steps: Add FluentProvider at the root; keep v8 ThemeProvider until fully migrated.
Bridge theme (createV8Theme or a generated v9 brand theme).
Migrate incrementally using the mapping; replace hardcoded styles with tokens (fluent_get_token).
Wrap v8 islands in PortalCompatProvider for themed v9 overlays.
Verify each migrated screen (fluent-design-review + fluent_accessibility_checklist); remove shims as you finish.
gotchas: Shims increase bundle size (both v8 + v9 loaded) - use temporarily.
v9 has no Stack - replace with flex + spacing tokens.
Portaled v9 components lose theme without PortalCompatProvider inside a v8 tree.
Some v8 components have no 1:1 v9 (e.g., GroupedList) - re-compose with v9 primitives.
docs: https://react.fluentui.dev (Concepts > Migration from v8; v8 component mapping)

fromOtherDesignSystem.title: Adopt Fluent 2 in an app using another design system (MUI, Chakra, Ant Design, Bootstrap, plain CSS)
fromOtherDesignSystem.summary: Introduce Fluent 2 incrementally at a boundary and migrate screen-by-screen; there is no automated converter, so map components + tokens deliberately.
fromOtherDesignSystem.approach: Wrap a route/subtree in <FluentProvider theme={webLightTheme}> and build/replace that area with Fluent 2 components. Avoid mixing two design systems in the same component. Map your palette to a Fluent brand theme (fluent_generate_theme) and your spacing/typography/radius to Fluent tokens (fluent_get_token). Replace components using fluent_search_components / fluent_get_component.
steps: Pick a screen/route to convert first (lowest risk, high visibility).
Add FluentProvider at that boundary; generate a brand theme from your primary color.
Replace that screen's components with Fluent 2 equivalents (search the catalog).
Swap hardcoded colors/spacing/radius for tokens.*; verify a11y.
Repeat screen-by-screen; keep the two systems isolated per subtree until done.

hardcodedToTokens.title: Replace hardcoded colors/spacing/radius/shadows with Fluent 2 tokens
hardcodedToTokens.summary: The highest-ROI adoption step in any codebase: map magic values to Fluent design tokens so light/dark/high-contrast and theming just work.
steps: Inventory hardcoded values (hex, px paddings/margins, radii, box-shadows, font sizes).
For each, find the nearest Fluent token with fluent_get_token / fluent_list_tokens.
Replace with tokens.* (Griffel) or var(--tokenName); wrap in FluentProvider so they resolve.
Re-check contrast + high contrast; run fluent-design-review.

powerbiReport.title: Apply Fluent 2 to an EXISTING Power BI PBIP/PBIR report and repair the layout distortion it causes
powerbiReport.summary: A Power BI theme sets DEFAULTS: it only styles a property that a visual has NOT overridden inline. In real reports 68 to 95 percent of visuals carry inline overrides (visual.visualContainerObjects: background, border, visualHeader, title) for exactly the properties the Fluent theme sets, plus inline fontFamily/fontSize that defeat textClasses. Registering a theme therefore changes almost nothing on its own. THE JOB IS: register the theme, then DELETE the inline overrides the theme owns so its values apply. Never re-tint an override to a Fluent hex value; that leaves the theme inert and is the classic false success. Layout repair is a secondary phase that is usually empty, because applying a custom theme as files does not move visuals. See the fluent-powerbi-adopt skill.
powerbiReport.evidence: Measured across four real reports (2,249 visuals): 68%, 80%, 84% and 95% of visuals carried theme-defeating inline overrides. In one 1,243-visual report that was 2,596 overridden properties across 840 visuals (background 748, border 714, visualHeader 607, title 521), plus 545 visuals with inline fontFamily and 644 with inline fontSize. Applying a custom theme to it changed zero geometry (out-of-bounds 0 to 0, overlaps 244 to 244), confirming that layout distortion is not the failure mode. Microsoft states the rule directly: 'Reset to default doesn't affect styling you set on individual visuals from the formatting pane.'
powerbiReport.tools: Use the deterministic tools rather than hand-editing (a real report is 1,265 files and about 1.5M tokens to read): fluent_pbir_audit (baseline census), fluent_pbir_apply_theme (write + register with a computed reportVersionAtImport), fluent_pbir_normalize_inline (delete the overrides the theme owns; dry-run first; returns a full ledger), fluent_pbir_verify (assertions incl. the theme-effectiveness ratio).
powerbiReport.successCriterion: Theme-effectiveness ratio per theme-owned key = 1 - (data visuals with an inline override for that key / data visuals). Target 0.90 or higher on border, background, title and visualHeader. Print the matrix before and after. Counting pages/visuals/bookmarks cannot detect this failure: a run that changes nothing passes it.
powerbiReport.inlineOverrideShape: Theme JSON uses plain values: "border": [{ "show": true, "radius": 8 }]. PBIR inline overrides wrap every value in an expression literal: "visualContainerObjects": { "border": [{ "properties": { "color": { "expr": { "Literal": { "Value": "'#E6E6E6'" } } }, "radius": { "expr": { "Literal": { "Value": "0D" } } } } }] }. Strings are single-quoted inside Value, numbers carry a D suffix, booleans are true/false. Deleting the property (and the card when it becomes empty) hands control back to the theme. Never touch visual.objects (data-role formatting).
powerbiReport.whenApplies: The report must be PBIR: a *.Report folder with a definition/ folder that contains pages/. This is file-editable. It does NOT apply to a binary .pbix or PBIR-Legacy (a single report.json holding the whole model); convert first in Power BI Desktop (Options > Preview features > enable 'Store reports using enhanced metadata format (PBIR)', then re-save).
safetyRules: Never edit the semantic model. Themes and layout live in the report layer only; no measure, column, DAX, or relationship changes.
Never edit without a restore point (a clean git working tree, or a full copy of the *.Report folder).
Never change any name, id, GUID, object name, pageBinding.name, or $schema value. Bookmarks, navigation, drill-through, and tooltips cross-reference these and break silently when renamed.
Never fix an overlap you have not classified as unintentional. Many overlaps are deliberate (bookmark toggle groups, background shapes, buttons over cards).
Never move or resize a bookmark-controlled visual without updating every affected *.bookmark.json, or the bookmark snaps it back.
Never produce invalid JSON. Every file must still satisfy the $schema declared at its top.
Never batch-move visuals to solve overlaps. Apply the smallest change that resolves each issue.
workflow: Safety and baseline: confirm git is clean or copy the whole *.Report folder to a timestamped backup, then run fluent_pbir_audit and keep the output as the baseline.

Acquire and validate the theme: generate with fluent_generate_powerbi_theme or use the user's theme JSON. Verify it parses, has a reportThemeSchema $schema, and that its internal 'name' is the theme you intend. Registering a different theme than intended is a real failure mode.

Apply the theme with fluent_pbir_apply_theme: it writes StaticResources/RegisteredResources/<name>.json, APPENDS the CustomTheme item to the EXISTING RegisteredResources package, sets themeCollection.customTheme, and computes reportVersionAtImport as {visual: max visualContainer version, page: max page version, report: the report.json $schema version}.
Census the inline overrides: run fluent_pbir_normalize_inline with policy 'report' (dry run) to see exactly how much of the theme is being defeated and where.

Clear the overrides the theme owns: re-run with policy 'theme-wins' and dryRun false. Review the ledger (file, visual, key, property, before, after, reason). Visuals whose formatting a bookmark captures are reported rather than changed unless you opt in.
Update bookmarks that captured formatting: bookmarks store explorationState.sections.<page>.visualContainers.<name>.singleVisual.objects and will snap the old styling back if left stale.
Verify with fluent_pbir_verify and print the theme-effectiveness matrix before and after. Do not claim success until the ratio clears 0.90 on theme-owned keys and the identifier assertions pass.
Layout check (usually empty): re-run the audit's geometry findings against the baseline and fix only regressions your change actually introduced.

Report: theme applied and where registered, restore point, before/after effectiveness matrix, ledger summary, bookmarks updated, anything skipped and why, identifier integrity check, and a request to confirm visually in Power BI Desktop.
powerbiReport.effectMapNote: The effects below belong to the Fluent 2 BASE theme, which can only be switched on in Power BI Desktop (Options > Preview features > 'Modern visual defaults and customize theme improvements', then View > Themes > Customize current theme > Base theme). They do NOT occur when a custom theme is applied as files. Treat this as a checklist for users who also switch the base theme, not as the expected outcome. Because the base theme cannot be set from files, the custom theme must carry the entire Fluent 2 structural look itself.

effectMap.change: Increased padding and rounded corners on all visuals
effectMap.risk: Content area shrinks, so content clips and tight neighbors collide on render.

effectMap.change: Titles and subtitles on by default (axis titles off)
effectMap.risk: Added header height pushes content down, so it overflows or clips.

effectMap.change: Slicers change mode (list to dropdown or tile)
effectMap.risk: Footprint height or width changes, so slicers overlap neighbors.
Space requirement changes, so the visual overflows or leaves gaps.

effectMap.change: Buttons and navigators restyled; button fill uses the first data color
effectMap.risk: Nav bars misalign and button size or spacing shifts.

effectMap.change: Cards use less padding and no reference-label background
effectMap.risk: Card content re-anchors and alignment with neighbors drifts.

effectMap.change: New pages default to 1920x1080 (existing pages keep their size)
effectMap.risk: Out-of-bounds checks must use each page's actual width and height, not the new default.

effectMap.change: Uniform fonts and sizes across visuals
effectMap.risk: Text reflows, wraps, or clips where labels were tightly fit.

detectionRules.outOfBounds: x < 0 || y < 0 || (x + width) > page.width || (y + height) > page.height, using each page's own page.json width/height (1280x720 initial page, 1920x1080 new Fluent 2 pages). Tolerance about 1px for float rounding. This is the only test grounded directly in the schema (VisualContainerPosition semantics: x+width should be less than the page width, y+height less than the height).
detectionRules.overlap: Axis-aligned boxes A,B intersect when A.x < B.x+B.width && B.x < A.x+A.width && A.y < B.y+B.height && B.y < A.y+A.height. Flag as unintended only when same or adjacent z, not in the same visualGroup, and the overlap area exceeds about 25% of the smaller visual (heuristic).
detectionRules.collisionOnRender: Fluent 2 grows each visual's visible footprint by roughly borderWidth + shadowDistance + shadowBlur + shadowSpread per edge. Flag adjacent visuals whose inter-box gap is under about 8 to 12px even if the boxes do not intersect (heuristic; exact Fluent 2 shadow defaults are not published).
detectionRules.headerOverflow: Fluent 2 forces titles and subtitles on. Reserve a title band of about 24 to 32px (title 12pt / largeTitle 14pt, plus subtitle if present) and flag a visual whose content height leaves under about 4px of slack (heuristic; depends on font metrics).
detectionRules.typeBasedReflow: Slicer mode switch, small-multiple reflow, and button restyle change rendered content rather than stored geometry. Detect them by type and preset transition, then re-run the geometry tests and treat any newly triggered flag as theme-induced.
detectionRules.exclusions: Exclude background shapes and images (lowest z, page-spanning), currently-hidden visuals (visual.json isHidden), and grouped children (evaluate them through their parent).

neverRename: Every file's $schema (a wrong report.json $schema is a blocking error).
page name (referenced by pages.json pageOrder/activePageName/landingPageName, bookmark activeSection/sections, and navigation).
pageBinding.name (referenced by drill-through and page tooltips; must stay unique).
visual name (referenced by bookmark targetVisualNames and group parentGroupName).
visualGroup container name and members' parentGroupName (preserve groups).
bookmark name (referenced by bookmarks.json order and children).
Do not alter position.z (z-order) or position.tabOrder (tab order) during geometry repair unless intentionally fixing them.
powerbiReport.pbirFieldNotes: visual.json required fields are only $schema, name and position. The visual node is OPTIONAL: roughly 1 in 4 visual.json files carries visualGroup and NO visual node, so never assume visual.visualType exists. A visual's hidden flag is isHidden (boolean), NOT a visibility enum (visibility is a page-level field), and group membership is parentGroupName, NOT group. Container styling the theme owns lives at visual.visualContainerObjects; data-role formatting lives at visual.objects and must not be touched when normalizing. report.json themeCollection.customTheme uses type RegisteredResources and requires reportVersionAtImport as an object {visual, page, report}; APPEND the CustomTheme item to the EXISTING RegisteredResources package (real reports already have one holding images) and keep customTheme.name equal to the item name (item name without .json, path with it). Schema versions drift WITHIN one report (one report held visualContainer 2.5.0, 2.7.0, 2.8.0, 2.9.0 and 2.10.0 simultaneously; newer reports use 2.11.0), so compute the max rather than assuming one version. page.json also carries visualInteractions[] (cross-filtering) and filterConfig; bookmarks capture FORMATTING at explorationState.sections.<page>.visualContainers.<name>.singleVisual.objects. Canvas sizes are arbitrary per page (1350x1142, 1350x4423, 1850x1537 all occur): never assume 1280x720 or 1920x1080. In PBIR, definition/report.json IS externally editable and adding a new CustomTheme resource is supported; the Learn note about a non-editable report.json refers to the PBIR-Legacy root file that PBIR replaces.

perSurface.powerbi: A theme only styles properties a visual has NOT overridden inline, so registering a theme is not enough: in real reports 68 to 95 percent of visuals carry inline visualContainerObjects overrides for exactly the properties the Fluent theme sets. For a NEW report, generate with fluent_generate_powerbi_theme and apply via Power BI Desktop > View > Themes > Browse for themes. For an EXISTING PBIR report, run the 'powerbi-report' scenario (fluent-powerbi-adopt skill): audit, apply the theme, clear the inline overrides the theme owns, then verify with a theme-effectiveness ratio. Never re-tint an override to a Fluent hex; delete it so the theme applies.
perSurface.powerapps: In an EXISTING canvas app: Settings > Updates > New > enable 'Modern controls and themes', set App.Theme from your brand, then replace classic controls with modern equivalents screen-by-screen (see fluent-powerapps).
perSurface.powerpages: On an EXISTING site: add a custom CSS file that declares Fluent 2 tokens as :root variables and maps Bootstrap selectors onto them (see fluent-powerpages) - no rebuild required.
perSurface.pcf: Rebuild a legacy virtual control with a current CLI to pick up Fluent v9 platform libraries + context.fluentDesignLanguage theming (see fluent-pcf-component).
